tested_scope.question: Whether reachable Git history/object identity can serve as an enforceable fail-closed retention invariant for deterministic operation-key duplicate suppression when branch-protection/ruleset authority, richer-mode execution, paid or finite quota, and manual user execution are excluded.
tested_scope.method: Bounded semantics check against authoritative public GitHub branch-protection documentation and upstream Git object/reflog pruning documentation; no force-push, branch-rule, scheduler, protected-primary, or historical-checker execution was performed.
tested_scope.not_tested: No live destructive history rewrite was performed; this slice establishes a mechanism-level boundary from documented semantics, not empirical repository-host retention timing.

public_evidence.observed_semantics: GitHub documents branch protection as the mechanism that disables force pushes and branch deletion by default; it also states that force pushing may remove commits from branch history.
Git documents expiry of reflog entries, including a default shorter expiry for entries unreachable from the current branch tip, so reflog retention is not an immutable reachability guarantee.
Git documents pruning of unreachable objects and allows pruning grace periods to be shortened to immediate pruning, so object presence after loss of all protecting refs is not an invariant.
Git defines pruning in terms of objects unreachable from refs, confirming that retention is tied to reachability rather than immutable object identity alone.

result.finding: The candidate cannot establish reachable-history/object retention as an unconditional Chat-native invariant under the allowed route. Preventing history removal requires protection/ruleset authority or an equivalent independent immutable retention mechanism; absent that, a force-update or ref loss can make prior commits unreachable, and Git semantics permit unreachable reflog entries/objects to expire or be pruned. Therefore a later HEAD/path-history miss cannot fail-closed distinguish never-created from created-then-deleted-or-rewritten in all allowed states.
result.supported_property: The prior slice remains valid only for the exact case where the relevant creation commit lineage is still reachable: path-filtered history plus historical-ref readback can recover prior existence after working-tree deletion.
result.rejected_generalization: Reachable-history recovery must not be generalized to unconditional ABA resistance, ambiguous-write reconciliation, or duplicate/conflict safety when history reachability itself is not protected.
